summary: Iteration 38 focused multi-service testing completed against the public URL. Backend passed 6/7 cases: empty/oversized carts, unknown service atomic preflight rejection, insufficient balance, required comments, and single-order regression all passed. The required real+manual two-service success failed because the automated provider item returned a per-item failure, leaving only the manual order placed/charged. Frontend multi-cart UI passed toggle, Add/Remove, editable quantity, live total/enabled CTA, expected POST payload, and partial-result OK/FAIL rendering. Single-service UI still submits successfully, but its manual-order success message displays an undefined order ID.

critical.issue: The required automated service 7242 + manual service -1 request returned HTTP 200 but placed=1, failed=1 instead of placed=2, failed=0. The provider-backed item failed, so only the manual order was persisted/debited.

ui_bugs.issue: After a successful manual order, the toast and last-order banner show an undefined order ID (toast: 'Order placed! ID #undefined'; banner: 'Order ID # · charged $15.99').

integration_issues.issue: The UI correctly dispatched both catalog services, but the live response was partial success (1 placed, 1 failed) because service 7242 was rejected by the external provider. The cart correctly remained and the result panel listed OK/FAIL.

action_items: Restore/configure valid SMM provider credentials or curate an automated service that the provider accepts, then retest the required 2/2 multi-order success and persistence/debit assertions.
Return order_id for manual POST /api/client/order-with-balance responses or render a manual-specific success message without an order ID.
Clarify the product's 'atomic' promise: current endpoint intentionally allows partial provider failure and charges successful items rather than all-or-nothing fulfillment.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1991 describes the endpoint as atomic, but lines 2033-2119 sequentially continue after provider failures and debit successful items; this is partial-success semantics, not transactional all-or-nothing atomicity.
server.py:1906 omits order_id and smm_order_id from the manual single-order response, while ClientDashboard.jsx:2826-2827 always reads both, directly causing the reproduced undefined ID UI.
ClientDashboard.jsx renders manual catalog rows as $0.000/1000 even though checkout charges price_flat=$15.99; this pricing presentation is misleading before selection/cart entry.
server.py (7,260 lines) and ClientDashboard.jsx (4,474 lines) remain far above the 700-line maintainability threshold and should be split into focused routers/components.
Frontend lint still reports 38 pre-existing errors/warnings in ClientDashboard.jsx, including empty catch blocks and unescaped apostrophes; no new syntax error was found in the multi-cart area.

success_rate.frontend: 92% of executed focused assertions passed; multi-cart behavior passed, provider-backed 2/2 success failed, and single-order success messaging has an undefined ID

seed_data_creation: Temporarily inserted one expensive manual service and one custom-text service for validation; both were cleaned. Temporarily topped up testbugfix1 when needed. Live tests created manual orders/debits for backend and UI flows; test-created records were cleaned. The real automated provider did not accept the order, so no provider order cost was incurred.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/test_iteration_38_multi_order.py only; do not rerun iteration 37. Public catalog currently has automated IDs 7242 (min 50) and 7545 (min 100), plus manual -1 at flat $15.99. The UI successfully posts {7242:50,-1:1}, then renders 1 placed/1 failed. Retest after provider configuration is repaired. The initial /client/login test assumption was corrected: auth is the GuestLanding inline modal on /client/dashboard.
rca_of_the_issue: The core 2/2 failure is downstream-provider rejection: the endpoint preflights pricing and balance correctly, calls the provider sequentially, converts the rejected automated item into an item-level failure, then continues to persist/debit the manual item. The single-order undefined ID is a response/UI contract mismatch: manual order response returns no order_id/smm_order_id, but the UI unconditionally interpolates both fields.
